## Run the same source file

[View the complete `JmmLab.java`](examples/JmmLab.java). Compile with `javac JmmLab.java` from the `examples/` directory and run `java JmmLab volatile`. The example uses Java 17+ APIs; the normative specification baseline is Java SE 27.

**Official specification:** [JLS §17.4.4–§17.4.5](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se27/html/jls-17.html#jls-17.4.5)

## 1. Extend the same order desk

The first order desk could not safely communicate a stop request. Change its signal to `volatile` and add a readiness flag:

```java
static final class VolatileOrderDesk {
    int latestOrder;
    volatile boolean hasOrder;
    volatile boolean running = true;

    void submit(int id) {
        latestOrder = id;
        hasOrder = true;
    }
    void stop() { running = false; }
}
```

The worker waits until `hasOrder` is true, reads `latestOrder`, then later observes the stop signal. See `volatilePublication()` in the single source file.

## 2. Why publication works

The controller writes `latestOrder=102` **before** the volatile write `hasOrder=true` (program order). That volatile write synchronises-with a subsequent volatile read of the same field in the synchronisation order. The worker's later ordinary read of `latestOrder` is ordered after its observed readiness read.

By *transitivity*, the earlier ordinary write is visible to that worker read. We have an actual ordering argument, not just a hope that a CPU cache was refreshed.

## 3. Why stopping works

A volatile write of `running=false` and subsequent volatile reads establish the corresponding ordering. In this example the worker's loop is a simple cancellation signal.

This does not mean a busy-spin loop is a suitable design for production. In real applications, use blocking queues, interruption, executors, or other coordination primitives appropriate to the work.

## 4. What volatile does not do

```java
volatile int processed;
processed++;  // read + calculate + write: NOT one atomic operation
```

Two threads can read the same old value and write the same incremented value. A volatile variable provides individual access ordering/visibility properties; it does **not** make arbitrary read-modify-write expressions indivisible.

Likewise, a volatile reference does not make all the fields of the referenced object independently thread-safe. You must reason about the whole access protocol.

## 5. Exercise

Trace the edges from `latestOrder=102` to the worker's read. Then explain why replacing `hasOrder` with an ordinary boolean removes the required guarantee.

## Check your understanding

Explain which operations establish a happens-before relationship in this chapter. Distinguish a language guarantee from behaviour that merely happened in one execution.
